blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Leading remote and hybrid teams at the executive level is a deliberate design problem. In a fully co-located team, a lot of information flows accidentally: overheard conversations, corridor chats, shared lunches. When people are distributed, those accidental flows disappear. Unless the leader rebuilds them intentionally, the team slowly fragments — without anybody being able to point at when it started.

Although the tools matter, the deeper work is cultural. Provided that senior leaders write down how the team will communicate, how decisions will be recorded, how meetings will end, and how time will be protected, the team can thrive across distance. Without those rules, the team defaults to whoever happens to be most comfortable in the tools — which is rarely the whole team.

Hybrid and remote leadership is harder than co-located leadership in one specific way: it leaves no room for implicit habits. Every habit has to be explicit, or it quietly stops existing. The leaders who accept that reality produce remote teams that outlast the trend that created them.

items.q: According to the text, how does much information travel in a co-located team?
options: Accidentally, via corridor chats and overheard conversations
items.why: "a lot of information flows accidentally: overheard conversations, corridor chats, shared lunches."

items.q: What does the text say happens if a leader does NOT rebuild those flows intentionally?
options: The tools take over the culture
items.why: "Unless the leader rebuilds them intentionally, the team slowly fragments."

items.q: According to the text, what is the deeper work of remote leadership?
options: Cultural work — writing down how the team operates
items.why: "Although the tools matter, the deeper work is cultural."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Explicit rules help a team thrive across distance.
The right software, on its own, will hold a remote team together.
Implicit habits tend to disappear when a team goes remote.
A distributed team can fragment without anyone noticing when it began.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que as ferramentas importam menos que a cultura — o software sozinho não sustenta o time.

items.q: The phrase "teams that outlast the trend that created them" suggests that…
options: remote work is only a passing fashion for these teams
trends are the main driver of team performance
good remote practices become durable, not just a reaction to circumstance
these teams will eventually return fully to the office
items.why: Inferência: quem trata os hábitos como explícitos constrói algo que sobrevive à moda que o originou — vira prática duradoura.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando como está reconstruindo a cultura do time remoto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, here's what I've been doing for the past month. I sat down and made a list of every single thing we used to do in the office without thinking about it — and there were far more of them than I expected.

Take the simplest example. In the office, if I walked past someone's desk and they looked stuck, I'd stop and help. That never happens on video, because I can't see anyone looking stuck. So I've made it explicit: every Wednesday, thirty minutes, anyone can drop in and say what they're blocked on. It's clumsy, but it rebuilds the corridor chat we lost.

The one that surprised me most was how meetings ended. In a room, you can feel a meeting close — people gather their things. On a call, it just stops, and half the team leaves unsure of what was decided. Now every meeting ends the same way: someone reads back the decisions and who owns them, out loud, before anyone drops off.

None of this is about the tools. It's about refusing to let a habit survive on the assumption that everyone remembers it. If it isn't written down, in a distributed team, it doesn't really exist.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did Sophie spend the past month doing?
options: Listing every office habit the team used to do without thinking
Reducing the number of weekly meetings
items.why: "I made a list of every single thing we used to do in the office without thinking about it."

items.q: How is Sophie rebuilding the lost 'corridor chat'?
options: A shared document listing everyone's tasks
A rule that cameras must always be on
Daily one-on-one calls with each team member
A weekly thirty-minute drop-in where anyone can say what they're blocked on
items.why: "every Wednesday, thirty minutes, anyone can drop in and say what they're blocked on."

items.q: What surprised Sophie the most?
options: How poorly the team communicated by email
How meetings ended on a call versus in a room
How many people preferred remote work
items.why: "The one that surprised me most was how meetings ended."

items.q: Why does Sophie now have someone read the decisions out loud at the end of a meeting?
options: Because the recording software is unreliable
Because on a call there is no natural signal that closes the meeting, so people leave unsure
Because the board requires formal minutes
Because she wants meetings to run longer
items.why: Inferência: numa sala dá para sentir a reunião fechar; na chamada não — então ela cria um encerramento explícito para todos saírem certos do que foi decidido.

items.q: What is Sophie's underlying principle?
options: Remote teams need fewer rules than office teams
Leaders should trust that everyone remembers the routines
The best tools will fix most remote problems
A habit that isn't written down effectively stops existing in a distributed team
items.why: Inferência: "If it isn't written down, in a distributed team, it doesn't really exist" — o explícito vence o implícito.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Half the team is co-located in London, and the rest work from home." Co-located means…
options: working in the same physical location
items.why: Co-located = no mesmo local físico — em oposição a distribuído/remoto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Those insights used to spread ___ over lunch; now nothing reaches the remote staff."
items.why: Accidentally = acidentalmente/sem intenção — o fluxo informal que se perde quando o time se distribui.

items.q: "We need to rebuild the informal channels we lost when the office closed." To rebuild means to…
items.why: To rebuild = reconstruir, estabelecer de novo o que se perdeu.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Without shared rituals, a distributed team can quietly ___ into disconnected individuals."
items.why: To fragment = fragmentar-se, esfacelar-se em partes desconectadas.

items.q: "Every implicit habit has to be made explicit, or it stops existing." An implicit habit is one that is…
options: understood and practised without being stated
items.why: Implicit habit = hábito implícito: praticado sem ser dito; o oposto de explícito (explicit).

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre liderança remota e híbrida. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's roll out the new meeting protocol team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, região por região ou time por time.

items.q: "A couple of managers pushed back on the always-on-camera rule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the drop-in sessions, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "The HR director still has to sign off on the remote-work policy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Buying nicer software won't move the needle on how connected the team feels." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não fará.
